memos.headline: Parabolic Leaders S05/S02/S03 Flash Overbought Warnings While S09 and S06 Break Down
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape today. S05 at RSI 84 and +40% above its 200-day mean is the most extended name in the universe—trend is undeniably powerful (+42% over 26 weeks, +18% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks) but the risk of a mean-reversion snap is elevated and I would not initiate new longs here. S02 and S03 are similarly stretched at RSI 80 and 75 respectively, both 18-20% above their 50-day means; I respect the momentum but prefer to wait for a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. On the weak side, S09 is in a clear downtrend with RSI 37, -15.7% from its 52-week high, and -13.8% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks—this is a name to avoid until it reclaims its 50-day mean. S06 and S01 are also lagging badly on a relative basis and trading below their 200-day averages, offering no technical reason to own them here.

views.note: RSI 84 and +40% above 200d mean is parabolic; trend is strong but risk/reward poor for new entries—would flip long on a pullback to ~325 (near 50d mean).
Massive 12w relative strength (+29.6% vs SPY) and near highs, but RSI 80 and +22.6% above 50d mean argue for patience; a close below 310 would negate.
Best 12w relative strength in the universe at +27% vs SPY with RSI 75 near highs; would add on any dip toward the 50d mean (~231) and stop below 225.
RSI 66 is healthier than the other leaders, +6.6% 12w relative strength, only -0.7% from highs; cleanest risk/reward among uptrending names, stop below 190.
RSI 37, -15.7% drawdown, -13.8% 4w relative strength—clear downtrend; would reconsider only on a reclaim above the 50d mean (~155).
Negative returns across all timeframes, -11.1% 4w relative strength vs SPY, below 200d mean—no reason to own; needs to reclaim 310 to reconsider.
Below both moving averages, -15.1% 12w relative strength vs SPY, RSI 50 with no momentum—dead money until it clears 155.
At 52-week highs with RSI 73 and +11.6% above 50d mean, but 12w relative strength is flat vs SPY; trend is fine but not a leader—would buy a pullback to 265.
Still -23.4% from 52w high and below 200d mean despite a +12% 4w bounce; this looks like a bear-market rally—avoid above 420, reconsider on a breakout past 450.
Extraordinary 26w return of +54% and +49% above 200d mean, but RSI 67 is more moderate; the extreme extension from the 200d makes new entries risky—stop below 800.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 deliver extraordinary margin expansion; S09 earnings collapse demands caution
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names where earnings power is compressing. S10 posted a 63.1% net margin on $68.1B revenue with YoY net income up 94.5% and only $8.5B of total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is similarly impressive at 56.9% net margin, +81.2% YoY net income growth, and minimal leverage ($14.8B debt on $109.9B revenue). On the other end, S09's net income fell 45.8% YoY to just $4.2B on $85.1B revenue, yielding a razor-thin 4.9% margin—I cannot pay for that trajectory. S02 is stagnant with only +2.0% revenue growth and flat net income, while carrying $77.9B in debt; I see no catalyst. I would revisit S09 if margins stabilize above 8% and S02 if revenue growth re-accelerates above mid-single digits.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, +94.5% YoY net income growth, and only $8.5B debt make this the strongest earnings profile in the universe.
56.9% net margin with +81.2% YoY net income growth and low leverage ($14.8B debt) signals durable, expanding earnings power.
38.3% net margin, +23.1% YoY net income growth, and manageable $40.3B debt support a high-quality compounder thesis.
Revenue of $181.5B growing 16.6% YoY with net income up 76.7% shows strong operating leverage, though $122.6B debt and 16.7% margin warrant monitoring.
Solid 26.6% margin and +16.6% revenue growth, but $82.7B total debt relative to earnings keeps me from high conviction.
+22.2% revenue growth and 14.6% margin are decent, but $36.2B debt on only $17.4B quarterly revenue is heavy leverage.
33.1% net margin is attractive but $448.8B total debt dwarfs the $49.8B revenue base; balance sheet risk tempers enthusiasm.
Steady 18.5% margin and +7.4% revenue growth are fine but unexciting; $23.9B debt on $21.2B quarterly revenue is manageable but not compelling.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on $85.1B revenue—clear cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Only +2.0% revenue growth, flat net income, 5.6% margin, and $77.9B debt signal stagnation with no visible earnings catalyst.

memos.headline: Fed on Extended Pause at 3.75% as Sticky 3.3% CPI Keeps Easing Off the Table
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months with no change, after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year. CPI running at 3.3% YoY—well above target—while unemployment holds steady at 4.3% gives the FOMC no urgency to move in either direction. The 10y yield has drifted up 16 bps over three months to 4.38%, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 23 bps to +0.49 pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and a flattening curve that historically pressures bank NIMs and duration-sensitive growth. The regime is late-cycle pause with above-target inflation and a stable but softening labor market—I favor defensive sectors (staples, energy) over rate-sensitive growth and banks. A CPI print dropping below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift my call toward imminent easing.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from a 4.38% 10y yield rising 16 bps in 3 months with no near-term rate relief.
Banks face NIM compression as the 10y-2y spread has narrowed 23 bps to 0.49 pp and the pause regime limits further curve steepening.
Staples benefit from a defensive tilt in a late-cycle pause with sticky inflation and stable unemployment at 4.3%.
Energy acts as an inflation hedge with CPI at 3.3% YoY and the Fed unable to ease, supporting real-asset positioning.
Cyclicals face mixed signals—stable employment supports demand but rising long rates and sticky inflation cap upside.
Rate-sensitive sectors remain under pressure with the 10y at 4.38% and no easing catalyst visible in the data.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S05 and S07 Lead Upside, S04 and S09 Flash Warning Signs
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. S05 (+10.0%) and S07 (+9.9%) posted the strongest positive reactions to their Q-end results, suggesting a decisive narrative shift to the upside that may still have momentum given the magnitude. S02 (+7.0%) and S08 (+3.2%) also reacted positively, though S08's earlier director departure filing on 4/20 introduces some governance noise I want to watch. On the negative side, S04 dropped -3.9% on its results release and S09 slipped -1.0% with a follow-on executive change filing on 5/4, which together signal deteriorating sentiment. S06 is the most complex name: a mildly negative earnings reaction (-0.8%) followed by a flurry of governance filings including a material modification to security-holder rights on 5/7, which could be a structural overhang that the market has not yet fully digested.

views.note: A +10.0% earnings-day pop is the strongest positive sentiment signal in the universe and likely reflects a genuine narrative upgrade.
Near-double-digit +9.9% reaction to results plus Reg FD disclosure suggests broad positive re-rating; multiple pre-earnings filings kept coverage volume elevated.
A +7.0% earnings reaction is solidly positive, though the filing is now nearly three weeks old so some of the sentiment lift may be priced.
Positive +3.2% earnings reaction is encouraging but a director departure ten days earlier adds governance uncertainty that tempers conviction.
A -3.9% drop on earnings is the worst reaction in the universe and signals negative sentiment momentum.
Mild -1.0% earnings miss compounded by a subsequent executive departure filing on 5/4 points to a souring narrative.
Slightly negative earnings reaction, followed by bylaws amendments and a material modification to security-holder rights on 5/7, creates governance overhang the market may not have fully priced.
Modest +1.7% earnings reaction and paired Reg FD disclosures suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment; no strong directional signal.
Heavy filing cadence but only a +0.8% earnings reaction implies the market had already absorbed the narrative from multiple Reg FD disclosures.
Only a director change filing with no earnings data yet; insufficient sentiment signal to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Oil at $98 and Policy Uncertainty Spiking Signal Geopolitical Supply-Chain Stress Across the Universe
memos.body: I see a bifurcated macro picture: VIX has collapsed 34% over the past month to 17.08 and HY spreads have tightened 33bp, suggesting markets are pricing calm, yet the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index surged 31% month-over-month to 318 and WTI crude has rocketed 54% over three months to $98.38/bbl. This divergence tells me markets are complacent about a structural energy-security and trade-policy shock that has not yet fully transmitted to equities. The flurry of Reg FD (7.01) filings across S03, S01, S09, and S07 in April–May suggests companies are proactively communicating with investors about policy-sensitive developments, which I read as management teams bracing for further disruption. I have higher conviction on names with heavy energy or supply-chain exposure and lower conviction where the 8-K content is opaque. A reversal in WTI below $80 or a meaningful de-escalation in the policy uncertainty index below 250 would change my view.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in five weeks including two Reg FD disclosures suggest management is navigating active policy headwinds; elevated oil and uncertainty indices amplify risk.
Three filings since late March including a May 1 Reg FD disclosure warrant monitoring, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view beyond noting policy sensitivity.
Three 8-Ks in three weeks culminating in a May 7 filing suggest active corporate developments; the tightening HY spread is supportive but the policy uncertainty spike keeps me sidelined.
Two Reg FD filings in April indicate management is front-running policy news; I stay neutral until the energy-cost pass-through picture clarifies.

Filing cadence is steady rather than panicked, and the VIX drop plus HY tightening suggest the market is giving S07 credit; I lean long but with moderate conviction given the macro uncertainty overhang.
No company-specific filings in the evidence set, but the 54% three-month oil surge and elevated policy uncertainty create an unfavorable backdrop for names with energy-cost exposure.
